The message is encoded in the **heights of the ten building silhouettes**, read left to right, with **A=1 … Z=26** applied to `height ÷ 10`, and **word breaks marked by wider gaps** between buildings.

All buildings share the same fill (RGB 22,27,46), are exactly 28 px wide, and all stand on the ground line at y=259. Measured tops/heights (the tallest building's 2‑px antenna and red beacon are separate shapes; its full‑width rect starts at y=30):

| x‑range | top | height | ÷10 | letter | gap before |

| 53–80 | 210 | 50 | 5 | **E** | 6 |

| 319–346 | 30 | 230 | 23 | **W** | 6 |
| 353–380 | 120 | 140 | 14 | **N** | 6 |

### What I ruled out
- **Lit windows** (45 identical 4×6 blocks, two columns per building): a hand‑drawn zig‑zag with irregular spacing; no consistent grid, and the lit/unlit bit matrices give no ASCII/Morse. No unlit windows exist in any other shade.

### Confidence
High (~95%) that the message is deliberately encoded and reads "MEET AT DAWN". This is an explicitly derivable encoding (exact multiples of 10, all within the alphabet range, coherent English, and word spacing confirmed by independent geometric cue), not an impression. The only residual uncertainty is interpretive (e.g., whether the stub buildings/gaps were intended exactly as I read them), not about the derivation itself.
